home.about: Professor Jianjiang Li works at USTB’s School of Computer and Communication Engineering. He is a doctoral supervisor and holds a Ph.D. in engineering from Tsinghua University. His research covers high-performance, parallel and distributed computing, cloud computing and big data, and integrated intelligent supercomputing applications. This site brings together public profile information and verified selected work.
home.focus: From multicore parallelism and program optimization to distributed data management and scientific software for applications such as materials simulation.
home.join_text: Learn about research directions for doctoral and master’s study. Eligibility, places and timelines depend on annual university and school notices and confirmation from the supervisor.
home.platform_note: The HPCDE public team directory lists Professor Li. The site describes a high-performance computing and data engineering laboratory at USTB and provides further context for the broader research platform.

join.heading: Explore the research and admissions arrangements
join.intro: Prospective doctoral and master’s students interested in Jianjiang Li’s group at USTB can start with the faculty profile and selected work, then consider their own research interests. This guide introduces preparation for enquiries and official admissions resources. Formal arrangements follow annual university and school notices and supervisor confirmation.

degrees.label: DOCTORAL STUDY
degrees.title: Doctoral applications
degrees.text: Professor Li is a doctoral supervisor. Read the selected work to learn about related research. Programs, application routes, eligibility and places must be checked against annual admissions documents and confirmed with the supervisor.

degrees.label: MASTER’S STUDY
degrees.title: Master’s applications
degrees.text: Explore parallel programming, distributed data management and scientific software. Degree categories, examination or recommendation requirements, and admissions plans follow the annual official notices.

steps.title: Explore the research
steps.text: Read the research themes and selected papers, identify systems questions that interest you, and consider how your background relates to the group’s work.

steps.title: Prepare for a conversation
steps.text: An enquiry email can briefly describe your background, questions of interest, project or research experience, and what you would like to learn. You may include a CV or public project links where relevant. These are communication suggestions, not formal application requirements.

steps.title: Check annual admissions notices
steps.text: Use the university admissions site and school notices to confirm programs, dates and formal procedures. Email correspondence does not replace an application.

faq.question: Are specific doctoral or master’s places confirmed?
faq.answer: This site has not confirmed the current annual admissions plan. Consult USTB graduate admissions resources, school notices and the supervisor for the relevant year. Research descriptions do not establish available places.

faq.question: Can I speak with a group student before applying?
faq.answer: Use the student contact entry at the bottom right to discuss research interests, group life and preparation for applications. Formal eligibility, assessment and admissions arrangements remain subject to official notices and supervisor confirmation.

faq.question: Does emailing the supervisor replace a formal application?
faq.answer: Email is for research discussions and enquiries; it does not replace an application. Follow the annual admissions documents for the application route, materials, dates and assessment process, and apply through the required channels.
